abstract: While salt and osmolyte effects on protein folding have been extensively characterized, their effects on the dissociation equilibria of protein complexes are less well understood. These effects arise from preferential solute interactions with functional groups exposed during unfolding or dissociation, as described quantitatively by the solute partitioning model (SPM). The surface exposed upon unfolding has a remarkably similar functional group composition among globular proteins, leading to broadly similar effects of a given solute on the unfolding free energy. In contrast, the composition of the surface exposed upon dissociation can vary substantially among protein assemblies, making solute effects dependent on the specific interface. Here, we use fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to characterize the trimer - monomer equilibrium of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) sliding clamp in 50-1000mM potassium chloride (KCl) and potassium glutamate (KGlu). KCl, generally a weak stabilizer of folded proteins, had a modest, nonmonotonic effect on PCNA dissociation, with weak stabilization at intermediate concentrations and partial destabilization at higher concentrations. KGlu, a strong stabilizer of folded proteins, progressively stabilized the trimer, decreasing the effective dissociation concentration approximately fivefold between 50 mM and 1000 mM. Kinetic measurements showed that this stabilization arises predominantly from an increase in the association rate constant. Analysis of the crystal structure and molecular dynamics simulations showed that PCNA dissociation exposes a surface enriched in amide oxygen and depleted in hydrocarbon relative to typical unfolding surfaces. Within the SPM, the distinct interactions of KCl and KGlu with these groups provide a molecular rationale for their contrasting effects on PCNA dissociation. These results demonstrate that trends established in protein folding studies cannot be assumed to extend to protein dissociation equilibria.

metadata.title: Contrasting Effects of Potassium Glutamate and Potassium Chloride on the Oligomerization Equilibrium and Kinetics of the PCNA Sliding Clamp

summary: Potassium glutamate stabilizes the PCNA trimer about fivefold via faster association, while KCl has a modest nonmonotonic effect, shown by FCS and MD.
title: Contrasting Effects of Potassium Glutamate and Potassium Chloride on the Oligomerization Equilibrium and Kinetics of the PCNA Sliding Clamp
